correctness.rationale: For 1<=a<b<c<d<e<527, prime 523 divides 527! once and no earlier factorial before 523, forcing e in {523,524,525,526}. Prime-valuation parity signatures turn the six-factor square condition into a XOR identity. Every sextuple admits one and only one strict two-pair join (a,b) with (c,d), so exhaustive enumeration of the four finite e-slices proves the entire result. Independently factored integers to build all factorial parity signatures, joined pair maps while enforcing b<c, and obtained N(523)=5, N(524)=0, N(525)=1, N(526)=126, total 132; verified the concrete first tuple (2,11,29,35,526,527) and sample (16,17,30,31,526,527). The actual source verifier uses independent Legendre valuations and reverse join plus a complete CSV certificate; I inspected these paths and the CSV data. No probabilistic or infinite inference is made.

value.rationale: The least index at which six distinct factorials are required is a natural extremal boundary of the Erdős–Graham problem. Exhaustively counting all 132 optimal witnesses, including near-complete concentration at e=526, is a concrete unknown exact invariant and a reusable benchmark for representation or sieve algorithms, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice. A general all-index theorem is not demanded for value; does not repackage known threshold as new.
